subject: DPA clarifications — controller/processor, subprocessors, breach notice
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Smith <dana.smith@orion-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call follow-up: DPA clarifications + next steps

Hi Dana —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the items you asked us to confirm so we can move the procurement thread forward: 

1) Controller vs Processor: confirm Redwood operates as a data processor for customer-supplied customer data; customers remain the data controller.
2) Subprocessors: you asked for a current subprocessor list and notification cadence for additions. Attached is the current list referenced in the DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf).
3) Breach notice timing: you asked whether Redwood can commit to 24-hour notification for incidents — we typically operate on a 72-hour disclosure for confirmed security incidents but want to discuss exceptions.
4) Model training and use of customer data: we do NOT use customer-provided PII to train models without explicit written consent and a separate agreement.
5) Data residency & retention: we can pin data to a region (US/EU) depending on the deployment and offer configurable retention windows; default logging retention is 30 days unless otherwise agreed.
6) Logging controls & access: we provide audit logs and role-based access; SOC2 report available upon request.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll share the DPA PDF and a brief security summary (attached).
- Please flag any redlines your legal team needs and we’ll loop in our legal/security (cc’d here) for a quick review.
- If helpful, happy to schedule a 30-minute legal/security sync this week.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf, security_summary.pdf

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0123

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifications we need from Redwood before we proceed to procurement: 

- Can you confirm Redwood’s role formally in the DPA (processor vs controller)? We need the specific clause language.
- Does Redwood ever use customer-supplied data to improve or fine-tune models? If so, we need opt-out language.
- Please provide the current list of subprocessors and how you notify customers of new subprocessors.
- For breach notice, our security team prefers a 24-hour initial notification for incidents involving PII. Is that feasible?
- We need the most recent SOC2 Type II report and any pen-test summaries you can share under an NDA.

If you can send proposed wording for the above, I’ll take to our legal team. We may need a short call with your security/engineering to sign off on retention and logging controls.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: DPA clarifications — Orion Analytics (please advise)

Hi Dev / Dylan —

Forwarding Dana’s note from Orion (below). They asked for specific DPA language and several security confirmations. Can you please advise on the recommended responses (short bullets we can send to the customer) and any redlines we should accept/deny? Items called out by the customer: 

1) Controller/Processor clause — we should confirm we are Processor. Please provide the canonical sentence to include in email and DPA.
2) Use of customer data for model training — confirm our stance and how to commit not to use customer data for training without a separate agreement.
3) Subprocessors — provide current list and how we notify customers of additions (notification window).
4) Breach notice timeline — customer requests 24 hours for PII incidents. Our default is 72 hours; can we agree to 24 for critical incidents with an SLA and clear definition?

5) SOC2 / penetration test evidence — what’s the process to share these under an NDA?
6) Data retention & logging controls — default retention windows vs customer-configurable; recommended wording.

I attached the current DPA we sent. If you can annotate and return suggested wording (or an annotated redline), I’ll share with Dana and offer a quick legal/security call.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA clarifications — Orion Analytics (please advise)

Marissa —

Thanks for the ping. Below are suggested, customer-facing bullets you can send back to Dana. I’ve also attached an annotated redline with specific clause edits (dpa_annotated_redline.docx).

Recommended responses (short):
- Controller/Processor: Redwood acts as a Data Processor. Suggested sentence for DPA: "For the purposes of this Agreement, Customer is the Data Controller and Redwood Inference is the Data Processor with respect to Customer Data received under this Agreement."
- Model training: Redwood will not use Customer Data (including PII) to train or improve models without explicit written consent and a separate agreement; this is non-negotiable for customers who require it.
- Subprocessors: Provide current subprocessor list (see attached redline / security summary). We commit to notifying customers of new subprocessors at least 30 days prior to onboarding, unless urgent security/availability needs require a shorter window (in which case we’ll provide immediate notice and remediation details).
- Breach notice: Our standard is to notify customers of confirmed incidents within 72 hours. We can agree to 24-hour initial notification for critical incidents that meet a defined severity threshold (e.g., confirmed exfiltration of PII) provided we have an agreed escalation process and SLA.
- SOC2 / pen tests: We can share SOC2 Type II report and executive pen-test summary once a mutual NDA is in place. Provide the customer with a secure S3/Share link after NDA.
- Retention & logging controls: Default logging retention is 30 days for request logs; aggregated telemetry retained 180 days. Customers can request custom retention windows or data deletion processes via contractual addendum. PII will be deleted upon verified customer request in accordance with agreed retention schedule.

Ask: please propose language that commits to a 24-hour initial notification only for critical incidents; avoid blanket 24-hour requirements. Also confirm whether the customer needs subprocessors to be listed in the DPA itself or if a referenced subprocessor list (link) is acceptable.

Recommended next step: send Dana the bullets above, attach the annotated redline, and offer a 30-minute legal/security sync to close the remaining items. Happy to join the call if you want.

-Dylan
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com
